1.d4 e6 2.c4 f5 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.g3 c6 5.Bg2.strategy: Brings the king to safety behind the fianchetto and connects the rooks. White keeps its plans flexible: the e5 outpost, a trade of Black's good bishop and a later central break are all still available against the closed Stonewall structure.

Puts the bishop on the diagonal that contests e5, the outpost White's knight wants, and aims it at the kingside. This is the more active way to set up the Stonewall, because the dark-squared bishop gets a real job before Black castles and plays for a kingside attack.
1.d4 e6 2.c4 f5 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.g3 c6 5.Bg2.name: Dutch Defence: Stonewall Variation, Modern Variation
1.d4 e6 2.c4 f5 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.g3 c6 5.Bg2.background: Interest in the Stonewall revived in the 1980s and 1990s, when Artur Yusupov, Sergey Dolmatov, Nigel Short and Simen Agdestein helped develop this version, with ...d5 played early and the dark-squared bishop on d6. It has stayed more popular than the traditional set-up with the bishop on e7.
